conventions.convention: Matrix dimensions are positive finite integers. Channels are complex-linear, completely positive under every finite ancilla extension, and trace-preserving on every matrix input; unitality is separate.
The Choi matrix is unnormalized and uses input-reference ⊗ output order: J(Φ)=Σij Eij⊗Φ(Eij). The zero map permits an empty Kraus family.
The trace pairing is bilinear, Tr(XC), with no inserted adjoint; rectangular trace cyclicity uses matching dimensions.

The Schrödinger GKSL Hamiltonian term is −i[H,X]/ℏ. H is Hermitian in joules, ℏ>0 is in joule-seconds, time is in seconds, and finitely many jumps have units seconds^(−1/2). An empty jump sum is zero; time-dependent coefficients are continuous on a compact interval.

Reduced dynamics uses a fixed environment density and the product preparation ρ⊗σE, with system first and environment second; no semigroup law or marginal-only assignment for correlated preparations is assumed.

Entropy uses the natural logarithm, zero eigenvalue contribution 0 log 0=0, and a positive scale kB in joules per kelvin. The pinching proof retains full AC through its explicitly conditional finite-mixture supplier.
The trace norm is Tr√(X*X), and the contraction claim applies to arbitrary complex matrix inputs, including zero and non-Hermitian matrices.

load_bearing.statement: For complex-linear Φ:Md(C)→Me(C), complete positivity is equivalent to J(Φ)≥0 and to a Kraus representation with q≤de matrices. The empty sum is allowed for Φ=0. For any such representation, trace preservation is equivalent to Σa Ka*Ka=Id.

A finite channel has a unique bilinear trace dual, with Kraus formula Φ†(A)=Σa Ka*AKa; this dual is completely positive and unital. Composition, finite convex combinations and induced-norm limits preserve channels. Fixed-dimension induced-norm limits preserve complete positivity.
For a finite GKSL generator with the stated units and conventions, Tt=exp(tL) is a finite channel for every t≥0, T0=id, Tt+s=Tt∘Ts, and the family is norm-continuous.
For A∈Me×d(C) and B∈Md×e(C), Tre(AB)=Trd(BA). If Trd(XC)=0 for every X∈Md(C), then C=0.
For finite system and environment spaces, Hermitian total Hamiltonian and fixed environment density σE, Φt(ρ)=TrE(Ut(ρ⊗σE)Ut*) is a finite channel for every real t.
For a finite channel Φ:Md(C)→Me(C), its trace dual satisfies ||Φ†(A)||∞≤||A||∞ for every A, and ||Φ(X)||1≤||X||1 for every complex matrix X.
A continuous finite GKSL family on a compact time interval has a unique propagator solving ∂tΛ(t,s)=Lt∘Λ(t,s), Λ(s,s)=id, and this propagator is a finite channel for s≤t.

published_dependencies.used_for: Completeness of finite matrix and linear-map spaces in exponential, averaging and propagator constructions.
Norm-convergent operator exponentials, differentiation, exponential law, bounds and quadratic remainders in GKSL and reduced-unitary proofs.
Norm-Riemann integration and the fundamental theorem in the semigroup-generator and continuous-propagator constructions.
Second-factor coordinate contraction in the reduced-unitary theorem and correlated-preparation and finite-bath examples.
Environment-basis independence of the coordinate partial trace used to construct reduced-channel Kraus operators.
Explicit inherited premise for entropy concavity and the published KL nonnegativity supplier.
Scalar phases in pinching and finite-bath calculations.
Phase multiplication, reciprocal identities and the finite root-of-unity average.
Exact order of the root of unity used in the pinching average.
Unit-modulus phases and the exact finite-bath coherence values.
Existence of a positive phase with exponential i in the finite-bath semigroup counterexample.
Directional binary KL formula in the strict amplitude-damping entropy comparison.
Strict positivity of binary KL for unequal probability laws, under its explicit AC premise.
Definition and value at zero of the damping exponential.
Strict positivity of the amplitude-damping exponential.
The damping parameter satisfies 0<exp(−γt)<1 for γ,t>0.

concerns.concern: The illustrative CNOT target is off-center: the circle is drawn at (1.38,0) with radius 0.12, while the vertical control line and vertical plus stroke are at x=1.5. Consequently the plus and control connection meet the circle's right edge rather than its center. The basis-permutation calculation is unaffected.

alerts.finding: Definition outcome 2 states: 'Its normalized post-click state is L_ab|a⟩/||L_ab|a⟩||=|b⟩.' Proof step 1.2 repeats the normalized-state assertion. The Gibbs-jump supplier permits w_ab=0, even with a connected positive-rate graph; then L_ab=0 and the displayed quotient is undefined. The normalization needs an explicit positive-rate or realized-outcome qualification. For example, a connected three-state path permits a zero rate between its endpoints.

seams_checked.note: The reduced-unitary theorem cites exactly the finite Hermitian-Hamiltonian unitarity clause of thm-qsm-dt-finite-unitary and identifies its draft status. Its own proof also derives unitarity directly from the norm-convergent operator exponential. Neither the supplier nor its consumer asserts reduced semigroup dynamics or equilibration.

Checked GKSL definitions and uses in the detailed-balance definition, gap theorem, Gibbs-jump theorem, monitored-chain definition, effective-bath postulate and open-Kubo theorem. Finite-dimensionality, Hamiltonian sign, jump units, forward-time CPTP conclusions, trace duality and continuous-coefficient hypotheses agree. The gap theorem's Schwarz and dual-norm citations are established in the trace-contraction proof. The bath postulate separately adopts physical applicability on its resolved finite interval; mathematical continuation is not presented as empirical evidence. The zero-rate normalization alert concerns the downstream definition itself, not a misstatement of a channels supplier.
